title: Using Cryo-Electron Tomography to Study the Molecular Mechanisms of Neurotropic Viral Infections Using Rabies as a Model System
content: Many different types of viral infections, such as rabies, Tick-born encephalitis virus, zika, and West Nile virus (WNV) can target human neurons, leading to severe neurological symptoms or death [1-3]. Other viruses, such as dengue and SARS-CoV-2, are known to have neurological effects, but how they target and infect neurons remains poorly understood [4, 5]. This results in a lack of effective therapeutic measures for many of these diseases to mitigate their neurological effects.
